name: Motorcycle
description: A road-registered motor vehicle with a seat and no more than three wheels that meets federal motor vehicle safety standards. Indiana draws no power or speed line for an electric motor: a street-legal electric two-wheeler that isn't an e-bike is a motorcycle unless it's registered as a motor driven cycle. Defined by Indiana Code §9-13-2-108; HEA 1200 (P.L.156-2026) lowered the endorsement age from July 1, 2026.
restrictions: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
No limit on motor power or speed; excludes electric bicycles and motor driven cycles

Built for highway use: meets federal motor vehicle safety standards (49 CFR 571) and Indiana's equipment rules, including brakes on both wheels, footrests and DOT lamps; an off-road e-moto without that certification is an off-road vehicle instead
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement, which takes a written and a skills test
The endorsement takes an age of 16 with an approved motorcycle safety course (16 years and 90 days before July 1, 2026), or 16 years and 270 days without one
A motorcycle learner's permit allows riding only in daylight, with no passengers and a DOT helmet
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a DOT motorcycle helmet and protective glasses, goggles or a face shield
Titled and registered with the BMV, and must carry liability insurance; an electric one also pays the electric vehicle supplemental registration fee
Headlamp lit whenever it's ridden; one passenger allowed on a seat built for one
